blocks.content: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935 in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935, based on the recommendations of the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance (Hilton Young Commission).
The legal foundation of the central bank was laid down by the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Initially established as a private shareholders' bank, RBI was nationalised on January 1, 1949 under the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 empowers the RBI to license, supervise, and regulate commercial banks across India.
Hilton Young Commission (1926) is frequently tested as the advisory body behind RBI's creation.
Differentiate between RBI Act 1934 (central banking functions) and Banking Regulation Act 1949 (commercial bank regulation).
Remember that Central Office was initially in Kolkata and permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
